Consumer brands, marketing organizations, and how a CMO thinks genuinely interest you — experience there is a plus, real curiosity is required. - You're collaborative, organized, thoughtful, and kind. Acquisition gets customers to italist once — your job is everything after that. You'll own customer loyalty, retention and re-engagement, and our owned channels: email and social. If a customer buys once and never comes back, that's on you; if they become a loyal repeat shopper who opens every email, that's on you too! This is a full-time, remote-first role in Canada, the US or the UK. THINGS YOU'LL WORK ON - Email & Lifecycle Marketing: you'll own our email program in Klaviyo end-to-end — the campaign calendar, trigger-based flows (welcome, browse and cart abandonment, post-purchase, winback), segmentation, testing and deliverability. Roughly 20% of italist's revenue comes from email today; you'll own that number and push it higher — and prove it with holdouts and incrementality, not just last-click attribution. - Retention & Re-engagement: you'll own repeat purchase rate — building the journeys that turn a first order into a second, and re-activating customers who've gone quiet. ATTITUDES We don't care what your current job title is, how long you've been working, or whether you've worked in luxury before. We do care about you being tightly aligned with our operating principles: - You're competitive and love to win. You're competitive and are always looking for an edge. jobgether-jobgether:lever:9dfea853-6a6a-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Program Manager, Data Governance and Stewardship based in the United States. This role will lead the development and ongoing evolution of data governance and stewardship practices across a complex, data-intensive organization. You will establish practical frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and accountability models that promote trustworthy and responsible data use. The position works closely with Data Strategy, Technology, Security, Legal, Compliance, and business stakeholders to strengthen data quality and governance. You will help improve data lineage, metadata, documentation, lifecycle management, and stewardship across critical data assets. The role also supports privacy, security, regulatory, client, analytics, automation, and AI-related data requirements. Success requires a balance of strategic thinking and hands-on execution, with the ability to influence stakeholders across functions. This is an opportunity to shape scalable data practices while promoting data literacy, accountability, and continuous improvement. Develop, document, maintain, and continuously improve data governance policies, standards, procedures, controls, and operating practices covering data collection, classification, storage, access, use, retention, and retirement. Establish clear data ownership, stewardship, accountability, decision rights, and quality responsibilities across business and functional teams. Partner with data owners, stewards, technical teams, and business stakeholders to implement governance standards, resolve data issues, and promote consistent adoption. Define data quality standards, rules, monitoring mechanisms, and remediation processes for critical data assets, while identifying root causes of errors, gaps, and inconsistencies. Maintain data lineage, catalogs, business glossaries, metadata, and supporting documentation to improve data traceability, understanding, accessibility, and lifecycle governance. Monitor adherence to data governance and quality standards, develop metrics and reporting, and communicate risks, findings, and remediation requirements to relevant stakeholders. Partner with Security, Legal, Compliance, Technology, Analytics, and AI teams to translate privacy, security, regulatory, contractual, and client requirements into practical governance controls. Support responsible data use across analytics, automation, machine learning, and AI applications by ensuring appropriate governance, privacy, security, quality, and documentation practices. Serve as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert on data governance, stewardship, data quality, and lifecycle management. Promote data literacy through clear guidance, documentation, training, and stakeholder engagement. Continuously refine governance practices as regulations, client expectations, business priorities, and technology evolve. Foster a collaborative, respectful, and solution-oriented environment while managing multiple priorities and maintaining strong follow-through. Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Data Management, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field preferred, or equivalent relevant experience. 5–8 years of professional experience in data governance, data stewardship, data management, data quality, or a closely related discipline. southparkcommons-boom-supersonic:ripplin.description: Senior Financial Accountant At most companies, a Senior Financial Accountant is a cog in a well-oiled close machine. The process exists, the templates are built, the checklist is handed over. Here, the function is still maturing while the business is moving. You will be expected to both execute core accounting work reliably and improve the systems around it in real time. Some processes will be undocumented. Some cycles will require triage. You will be expected to think, not just execute. The Mission Boom’s development of Overture will change how the world moves. The immediate development of the Superpower turbine will ensure we have the capital to make it happen. But none of this development happens without the financial infrastructure to support it. This role owns the general ledger and supports financial reporting — the foundation every investment decision, capital raise, and growth milestone is built on. Without reliable close and reporting execution, the company cannot scale responsibly or pursue the ambitions that make Boom worth working for. What you’ll do Execute month-end close end-to-end — journal entries, reconciliations, accruals, and variance explanations — every balance traceable, documented, and explainable at a business-driver level Support financial reporting and audit readiness by maintaining clean, well-documented workpapers and supporting schedules Identify recurring issues and manual workarounds and actively work to reduce or eliminate them, including through automation and AI tools Research, evaluate, and account for complex accounting areas and transactions, including equity, investments, interest, taxes, etc., resolving questions with confidence and clarity Manage and support the accounting systems and associated projects Support procurement, facilities, and legal teams through expert knowledge of the systems and great working relationships This job is demanding and rewarding Close and financial reporting cycles are time-pressured, and precision is non-negotiable even when things get messy. southparkcommons-profound:ashbyhq:c841ad.description: Profound is the marketing platform for the age of AI search. The way brands reach people is being rewritten — AI models like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Mode are now the answer layer between companies and their customers. We built the platform marketers use to understand, measure, and win in that world: the analytics, intelligence, and agent automation that turn AI search from a threat into a competitive advantage. We went from 0 to a $1B valuation in 18 months. Revenue grew 100x last year. Our customers include 15% of the Fortune 500 like Walmart, Wayfair and U.S. Bank, and innovators like Ramp, MongoDB, and Figma. We are backed by Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, LSVP, and Khosla Ventures — and we are moving fast enough that the people joining now are building the playbook everyone who comes after them will run. About the Role As our Head of Security you will build and lead the company's security program as it scales into a trusted enterprise platform. This is a foundational, high-impact role: you'll own security strategy end-to-end while staying hands-on, working alongside an existing Security Engineer to mature Profound's program from "does the right things" to "provably does the right things at enterprise scale." You'll also own IT for the company, making this a role that spans technical security leadership and the practical, day-to-day systems that keep the company running securely. This is a player-coach role. You should be comfortable setting strategy and talking to enterprise customers' security teams one day, and rolling up your sleeves on a threat model, an incident, or an endpoint policy the next. What You'll Do Security Strategy & Leadership - Own and evolve Profound's overall security strategy, roadmap, and risk posture as the company scales - Own the build-out and growth of the entire security function and team. - Serve as the executive-level owner of security in customer conversations, RFPs, and security reviews with enterprise and Fortune 100 prospects and customers - Partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Leadership to embed security into the SDLC and product roadmap Governance, Risk & Compliance - Own and mature Profound's compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II and beyond — e.g. ISO 27001, GDPR, and other frameworks as enterprise customers require) - Drive audits, policy development, vendor risk management, and control operations - Manage relationships with auditors, pen testers, and security vendors Technical Security - Provide technical direction and oversight for application security, cloud security (AWS/GCP), and infrastructure hardening - Own incident response: build the program, run tabletop exercises, and lead the response when needed - Guide and review the Security Engineer's work on detection, vulnerability management, and secure architecture - Evaluate and implement security tooling (SIEM, EDR, vulnerability scanning, etc.) IT - Own IT operations for the company: identity and access management (SSO/MDM), endpoint security, employee onboarding/offboarding, SaaS security posture, and internal tooling - Set and enforce IT policies that scale with headcount growth without creating unnecessary friction What We're Looking For - 8+ years in security, with progressively increasing scope, including experience owning a security program (not just executing within one) - Prior experience as a first or early security hire at a high-growth startup, ideally SaaS/B2B, strongly preferred - Hands-on technical depth — this is not a purely strategic/managerial role.
